o: We must repeatedly delete occurrences of '('×k + ')'×k (non-overlapping, left to right) and concatenate, until none remain. A single left-to-right stack pass reproduces this: whenever a ')' arrives and the top k stack entries are all '(', they annihilate and the ')' is dropped; newly exposed '(' can then be consumed by later ')' characters, exactly mirroring the cascade created by joining remnants. Examples confirm: '(())' with k=1 empties completely; '((()))()()()' with k=3 leaves '()()()'.
k: A stack pass where ')' consumes k '(' from the top emulates repeated leftmost removal in one scan.
Only the top k symbols ever matter, so membership checks are O(k).

a.i: Literally follow the statement: scan the string, delete non-overlapping k-balanced blocks, join, repeat until a pass deletes nothing. Easy to reason about but may run many passes.
s: Scan left to right; when s[i..i+2k) equals '('×k+')'×k, skip it and mark progress.
Join the survivors and loop until no deletion occurs.
a.t: O(n² / k) worst case — up to O(n/k) passes over the string

a.i: Keep characters on a stack. On ')', if the top k entries are all '(', pop them and discard the ')'; otherwise push it. Cascades caused by concatenation are handled implicitly because later ')' see the freshly exposed '('.
s: If ch is ')' and stack size ≥ k and the top k are all '(', pop k times; else push ch.
Join the stack for the answer.
a.t: O(n·k) — each character pushed once; each ')' checks up to k stack tops
